content.text:
I replaced all 7 `datetime.utcnow()` calls with `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` and added `timezone` to the `datetime` import in each file. The 5 changed files are `app/audit.py`, `app/billing.py`, `app/cache.py`, `app/reports.py` and `app/sessions.py`. No `utcnow` calls are left anywhere in the code.

The tests pass (5/5), including a run with `DeprecationWarning` treated as an error.

One visible change: `reports.header()` now ends its timestamp with `+00:00` (e.g. `2026-10-20T12:00:00+00:00`), because the times now carry a timezone. The test only checks the prefix, so it still passes, but anything that parses that header string exactly will see the new suffix.

All of `app/` now uses timezone-aware times, but code outside it can't mix the old kind in. If it compares or subtracts these times (`cache.Entry.expires`, `billing.due_date()`, session timestamps) with times that have no timezone, Python raises a `TypeError`. I didn't find any such code here.
